characters.description: The protagonist — a cheerful, curious learner navigating everyday life in Japan.
characters.bioLong: Rikizo grew up flipping through his grandfather's old kanji notebooks, convinced each character was a tiny locked door. Now he keeps a brush pen behind his ear and a vocabulary list in every pocket, treating daily life in Japan as one big open-book exam. He fails cheerfully, retries stubbornly, and celebrates every small win like a festival. His dream is to one day read those notebooks cover to cover without a dictionary.
characters.funFact: The 力 on his headband was his grandfather's seal — he re-inks it every New Year.

characters.description: Rikizo's good friend — a relaxed, easy-going companion who often runs into him around town.
A warm and kind teacher at Rikizo's school — widely regarded as the most gentle teacher.
characters.bioLong: Suzuki-sensei believes there is no such thing as a wrong answer — only an interesting first draft. Students who dread tests somehow leave her classroom asking for extra reading. She keeps a shelf of well-worn picture books she still swears by for teaching grammar, and she has never once raised her voice. Rumor says she once explained particle は so gently that the whole class understood it on the first try.
characters.funFact: She grades with a pale pink pen because red 'looks like shouting'.

characters.description: A kind and patient teacher at Rikizo's school.
characters.bioLong: Yamamoto-sensei has taught for thirty years and claims he has seen every possible kanji mistake — twice. His patience is glacial and his handwriting is museum-grade, and he will happily re-explain a stroke order for the tenth time as if it were the first. After school he tends a tiny bonsai on the staffroom windowsill that predates most of his students. Nothing delights him more than a learner who shows up again the day after failing.
characters.funFact: He writes the date on the board in perfect brush style every single morning.

characters.description: A close friend of Rikizo — upbeat and always up for celebrating.
characters.bioLong: Ken treats every minor victory as a national holiday: passed a quiz? Party. Learned a new word? Bigger party. He is the first to volunteer for karaoke and the last to leave, and he somehow knows every food stall owner in town by name. Beneath the confetti, he is fiercely loyal — when Rikizo wants to give up, Ken is already at the door with snacks and flashcards.
characters.funFact: He has a personal fanfare he hums whenever anyone finishes a lesson.

characters.description: A classmate who appears in early grammar practice conversations.
characters.bioLong: Yuki is the classmate who always seems to be in the right conversation at the right time — mostly because she starts them. She collects interesting sentences the way other people collect stickers, writing her favorites in a small notebook with a snowflake on the cover. New students gravitate to her because she asks easy questions out loud so nobody else has to. She insists winter is the best season and will debate anyone on it.
characters.funFact: Her notebook of favorite sentences is on volume seven.

characters.description: An international student from China learning Japanese in Japan — friendly and earnest, always trying his best.

characters.bioLong: Sakura runs the family kitchen like a friendly dojo: everyone helps, everyone tastes, and nobody leaves hungry. She quietly slips vocabulary cards under Rikizo's rice bowl when he forgets to study, then denies everything with a smile. Neighbors trade her homegrown vegetables for gossip, and she always comes out ahead on both. Her miso soup is legendary within a three-block radius.
characters.funFact: She can tell what mood Rikizo is in by how he says ただいま.

characters.description: A classmate of Rikizo — studious and thoughtful, often seen reading or studying Japanese.
characters.bioLong: Miki reads the way other people breathe — constantly and without noticing. She keeps three bookmarks going at once and can quote the exact page where she learned any word she knows. Quiet in a crowd but unstoppable in a study session, she is the friend everyone wants the night before a test. Her secret ambition is to write a story of her own someday, in Japanese, cover to cover.
characters.funFact: She alphabetizes her flashcards for fun and refuses to apologize for it.

characters.description: A diligent student who loves writing and never seems to rest.
A cheerful guy in his 20s who seems to work everywhere in town — always tired but always smiling.
A tall American English teacher with a Pacific Northwest vibe — long grey-streaked hair worn in a bun, always smiling regardless of what he's actually feeling inside.
A tall American exchange student who speaks decent Japanese but sometimes needs things explained. He always uses polite speech, no matter how casual the situation.
Rikizo's family shiba-inu — an energetic, cheerful dog who loves running and meeting people.
Owner of a factory in an industrial district.
A wise old tree Rikizo befriends and chats with — he's convinced 木さん is part of the family. Quiet, patient, and always listening.
Rikizo's pet goldfish — cheerful, curious, and a surprisingly good listener.
